target_customer: Bay Area transit riders (consumer, free app)
problem: Riders had to combine MUNI, BART and Caltrain information to find the best route right now.
business_model: Consumer app, no revenue model found

technical_complexity.rationale: Routing over public transit feeds plus real-time arrivals for three agencies; a Hacker News thread in 2013 noted BART was not yet supported.

defensibility.rationale: Built on public agency data with no lock-in; regional agency apps and large map apps could offer the same.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Not documented; no source on how incumbents reacted.

market_need_then: Not documented beyond the product description; a 2013 Hacker News thread discussed the app as combining routing with real-time Muni arrivals.

branding.domain_note: Product hosted on a subdomain, ride.roversf.com, per YC listing.

identity.voice_and_tone: Plain product copy on the YC page

brand_strength.rationale: Only a Hacker News thread and directory listings exist; the name Rover is shared with many unrelated companies.

outcome_analysis: RoverRide offered real-time SF transit directions across MUNI, BART and Caltrain from a single founder. No funding, traction or shutdown reason is public, and the company is listed as Inactive. The cause is not public, so no failure factors are assigned beyond what sources support.
notes: Site ride.roversf.com does not resolve (dead). Round Funded page is a reconstruction and was not used. Cause of inactivity not found. Competitors: a 2012 Bay Area 511 app and Google Maps transit existed but I found no source I could cite with a date, so the list is empty.
